clue.text: Investigated, holding back live work on code

indicators.note: the word for investigated keeps the turned-round piece held inside it

parts.note: dug, as in dug into a matter

indicators.note: back says the word for live is read in the other direction

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Someone investigated a problem while putting off live coding work.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove faults from a computer program is the standard programming term for fixing code.

clue.text: Around a month produces reworked section of wall

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged word outside the two short pieces
reworked says the letters of the word are shaped again into something new

explanation.surface: A month's work produces a rebuilt stretch of wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' makes DPCOURSE from PRODUCES, and 'Around' puts it round AM after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof layer built into a wall near the ground stops rising damp, so it is part of a wall.

clue.text: Obstruct poet endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly removes the last letter of the word for poet

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A command to block a poet who goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: To block or prevent passage is a direct synonym of obstruct.

clue.text: Player using energy needing a rest

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, as in full of go
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: A sportsperson running on energy needs a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The goalkeeper is one particular player in football and hockey.

clue.text: Pail may survive scrutiny

definitions.meaning: a sound bucket can contain liquid without leaking
an argument that stands up to examination is said to be sound and convincing

explanation.surface: A humble bucket is put on trial and comes through the examination.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an argument being sound literally describes a leak-proof container such as a bucket.

clue.text: Sit and cry — she must be suffering these?

definitions.text: Sit and cry — she must be suffering these?

indicators.note: suffering says the letters are in distress and so are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A woman sits weeping, so she must be in a state of uncontrolled emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncontrollable fits of crying or laughing are what a woman sitting sobbing might be having.

clue.text: Rising sea overwhelms very immature creature

indicators.note: the sea's name closes over the abbreviation for very, holding it inside
in a down clue rising means the sea's name is read upwards

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia

explanation.surface: A rising sea floods over a tiny young creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub or caterpillar is the immature stage of an insect before it changes form.

clue.text: Enormous weight placed on computer misuse

indicators.note: in a down clue, placed on puts the abbreviation for weight above the rest

parts.note: hacking is breaking into computer systems

explanation.surface: Huge emphasis is put on the misuse of computers.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for very large, as in a whacking great bill, means enormous.

clue.text: Let this out below — it may float away

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: down means below, as in down there

explanation.surface: An instruction to release something beneath that might drift off.
explanation.definitionFit: The feathery seed tufts of a weed are carried off on the breeze, so they may float away.

clue.text: Broadcast part in play that ham may fill

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard over the air rather than written

parts.note: a role is an actor's part in a play

explanation.surface: A hammy actor fills a role in a broadcast play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like an overacting actor, which fits the play, but it is meat in a bread bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bread bun can be filled with ham as a sandwich.

clue.text: Duck's little problem, back in lake and river

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for lake

parts.note: a mere is a small lake

indicators.note: back means the word for a little problem is read from its end

parts.note: a snag is a small hitch

explanation.surface: A duck has a minor difficulty somewhere on the lake or river.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander and red-breasted species are fish-eating diving ducks with serrated bills.

clue.text: Marie Lloyd is full of spirit on the stage

indicators.note: the name contains, running across its two words, the letters needed

explanation.surface: The music-hall star Marie Lloyd was bursting with liveliness when performing.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Lloyd was a famous British music-hall singer; 'spirit' points to drink or verve but means a sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's The Tempest has a sprite who serves Prospero, a spirit seen in theatres.

clue.text: Where slaves are sold at a monopoly price?

definitions.text: Where slaves are sold at a monopoly price?

parts.words: Where slaves are sold at a monopoly price?
parts.note: a literal market in captives, and the economic term for buyers with no choice of supplier who must pay what is asked

explanation.surface: A grim question about a slave auction where prices are set by one seller.
explanation.definitionFit: The economic term describes consumers locked into one supplier, here read literally as a sale of prisoners.

clue.text: Limits of endurance of a popular playwright engulfed by publicity

indicators.note: engulfed by puts the run of pieces inside the abbreviation for publicity

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
in means popular or fashionable
J M Barrie wrote Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A well-loved playwright is swamped by press attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes push through the point where effort becomes agony, the limits of their endurance.

clue.text: Fellow member, fit male, in condition

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the word for condition

parts.note: state means condition
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A colleague, a fit man, is in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse from the same yard, and by extension a colleague in the same organisation, is a fellow member.

clue.text: One time at college

indicators.note: at places the abbreviation for time next to the word for college, at its end

parts.note: uni is short for university

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a single occasion during their student days.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item or whole considered as one entity is a synonym of one.

clue.text: Where one may lay out sleeping bag purposefully?

definitions.text: Where one may lay out sleeping bag
definitions.meaning: a camper spreads a sleeping bag out with a canvas shelter around it, read as three words
deliberately, on purpose, as in the legal phrase for intending harm

explanation.surface: A camping question about where to unroll a sleeping bag, with a deliberate air.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into three words the answer says the bag goes with the camper under canvas; joined, it is the phrase meaning deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase for acting deliberately means doing something on purpose.

clue.text: Don't employ several solicitors to pursue argument to the end

definitions.meaning: read as four words the answer says have one tout, a tout being someone who solicits custom, so not several
to settle a dispute by arguing it out fully

explanation.surface: Advice to skip a team of lawyers and argue the case through yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as HAVE I TOUT, it means have one solicitor of custom; 'solicitors' suggests lawyers but means touts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have a frank confrontation that settles an argument.

clue.text: Shoddy fighter knocked over with sharp blow

indicators.note: in a down clue knocked over means the plane's name is turned upside down

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter plane
a crack is a sharp blow

explanation.surface: A poor-quality fighter is floored with a sharp punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap and flimsy showy trinkets are described as shoddy goods.

clue.text: Humble communication on boat

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the word for communication comes after the word for boat

parts.note: sub is short for submarine, a boat
a missive is a letter or message

explanation.surface: A modest message is sent aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Meek and yielding behaviour is humble in the sense of deferring to others.

clue.text: Go down badly for a lot of money

definitions.meaning: a show that flops is said to fail spectacularly
in British slang something costing a fortune costs this

explanation.surface: A costly venture fails with its audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Two informal senses: to flop, as a play does, and a fortune, as in costing the earth.

clue.text: Free to enter party that's got up for those recently joined

indicators.note: to enter places the word for free inside the turned party
in a down clue got up means the party abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A free party has been arranged for new members.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a bride or wedding means suited to a newly married couple.

clue.text: Incarcerate criminal and put in block regularly for obstinacy

indicators.note: put in places the picked letters inside the rearranged word
criminal suggests the letters of the word are in a corrupt, disordered state
regularly takes every other letter of the word block

explanation.surface: A call to jail a lawbreaker and hold him in a cell block because he will not yield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' reads as describing the prisoner but scrambles the word before it; 'regularly' picks letters two and four of block, and 'put in' sets them into the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn refusal to obey authority is a synonym of obstinacy.

clue.text: Restraint of girl leading to love

indicators.note: leading to puts the word for girl first, before the letter for love

parts.note: lass is a girl
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A girl's restraint leads to love.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's looped rope restrains cattle, so it is a type of restraint.

clue.text: Winter misery, standing around one platform

indicators.note: around puts the turned letters about the numeral for one
in a down clue standing means the abbreviation reads upwards

parts.note: SAD is seasonal affective disorder, a winter depression
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person stands miserable in winter round a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stage for a speaker or top table is a type of platform.

clue.text: Soul of a bird returning

indicators.note: returning says the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: the mina, also spelt myna, is a talking bird of the starling family

explanation.surface: A bird's soul comes back after death.
explanation.definitionFit: Jung's term for the inner self or soul, from the Latin word for breath or spirit.

clue.text: Park on downs for a ramble, taking main road back

indicators.note: taking the words for a ramble sends their letters wandering into a new order
back reverses the road's name

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered main road, its 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A walker heads off over the downs, then takes the main road home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a ramble' scrambles the two words into the Welsh mountain's name; 'back' turns the A1 road round, its figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh national park around the highest mountain in Wales is a well-known example of a park.

clue.text: Regularly insult head

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of the word insult

explanation.surface: Someone routinely insults the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for the head, as in use your noggin.

clue.text: Be dismissed in America, and start an independent course

definitions.meaning: in baseball a batter is out after three strikes
to set off on one's own path, often followed by on one's own

explanation.surface: An American who loses a job goes off to make their own way.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseball dismissal after three strikes, and the idiom for setting off alone.

clue.text: Hot drink with butter up each side missing

indicators.note: the word loses its letter at each end

parts.note: to butter someone up is to praise them insincerely

explanation.surface: A hot drink served with butter, missing its sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each side missing' drops F and R from FLATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky espresso coffee is a common hot drink in cafes.
